title: Writing Quadratic Functions
seo_title: Algebra I Writing Quadratic Functions Worksheets (TEKS A.6B, A.6C)
standard_text: A.6B write equations of quadratic functions given the vertex and another point on the graph, write the equation in vertex form (f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k), and rewrite the equation from vertex form to standard form (f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c); A.6C write quadratic functions when given real solutions and graphs of their related equations
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.6B and A.6C: write quadratic functions in vertex form from a vertex and a point, convert to standard form and write functions from zeros. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − h)² + k.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − h)2 + k, vertex (h, k).
  • Put the vertex in, then use another point to find a.
  • Standard form: f(x) = ax2 + bx + c. Expand the square to get it.
  • A zero at r gives a factor (x − r): zeros 3 and −5 give (x − 3)(x + 5).

Examples

Example

Vertex (2, −3) through (4, 5)

5 = a(4 − 2)2 − 3

8 = 4a, a = 2

Answer: f(x) = 2(x − 2)2 − 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong sign for hVertex (2, −3) gives (x − 2).
Finding a without squaringSquare (x − h) first.
Writing x + 3 for a zero of 3A zero of 3 gives (x − 3).
